extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; agency managers; OMB reviewers; federal personnel and facilities officials
extracted.subtask_description: Draft OMB circular establishing policy and requirements for federal employee parking: setting fees, exceptions, implementation timing, and agency responsibilities to encourage carpooling and transit use. Includes instructions for submitting written comments on the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a draft circular intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the [parking] space; the overall policy is intended to reduce subsidies for employee parking and to align with national energy conservation and public-transportation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission instructions and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite your written comments and ask that they be sent to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for notice-and-comment: comments must be written and submitted to the named official by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge commercially equivalent fees where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging commercially equivalent fees for parking would reduce the number of cars in the core regions; setting commercial-rate fees is a policy objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis for this requirement is empirical studies (e.g., WMATC, LA comparative study) linking user-paid parking to increased carpooling and transit use; fees should be comparable to commercial parking rates in the area to achieve behavioral change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis: fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking fees are to be based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fair market monthly rental value as the pricing metric so fees reflect commercial-equivalent costs rather than arbitrary amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception threshold for low rental-value locations
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small/rural/suburban locations with very low rental value may be exempt to avoid undue administrative burden or hardship; this threshold determines when charging is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fee level to recover costs and incentivize carpooling, without excessive administrative burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance required: choose a fee that (a) covers costs and creates an incentive to change commuting behavior and (b) does not result in administrative/management costs that exceed fee revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow a transition period so employees and agencies can make carpooling, transit and financial arrangements; implementation should be staged to reduce hardship and allow adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency affirmative plans where free parking continues
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for improving carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency chooses to continue free parking (e.g., due to low rental value exception), it must nonetheless produce and implement actionable plans to increase shared rides and vanpooling as mitigation and consistency with policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: More stringent application of carpooling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all applicable locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformly apply stronger carpooling rules (where appropriate) across Federal installations to increase carpooling rates; addresses current inconsistent application revealed by GSA surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goals and expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality are expected from this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these stated benefits as evaluative criteria for the success of the policy post-implementation; policy design should aim to achieve these measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure uniform application and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-wide carpooling regulations are not uniformly applied; survey shows uneven application (e.g., many single-occupant vehicle uses despite regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should include mechanisms (oversight, standard rules) to ensure consistent implementation and enforcement across agencies and locations to avoid inequities and loopholes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation expectation: carpooling and transit as cost-sharing alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging a commercial-rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship; employees will often be able to share the costs through carpooling or use public transit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supports/encouragement to form carpools/vanpools and use transit, and consider these modes when assessing hardship claims related to parking fees.
